paragraphs.text: [3~4] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.

Universal design is not only applied in modern architecture but also extends to transportation systems. For instance, buses have been designed with a floor closer to ground level to ease access for all passengers. Handles of various lengths are provided, another method by which universal design is implemented to accommodate passengers’ different heights. Subway maps have also been designed for color-blind individuals to clearly distinguish between subway lines by adjusting the color and the brightness and by varying the thickness of lines that have similar colors. ______(A)______, the use of pictograms can be seen frequently, Signs indicating the locations of subway or train stations assist international travelers who may not be familiar with the local language. ______(B)______, road signs indicating school zones, speed limits, and directions for turns and stops aid drivers in recognizing important information more easily.
윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
① Similarly		Thus
② Likewise		However
③ In addition		Likewise
④ Nevertheless		In short
⑤ On the contrary	In addition
윗글의 내용을 가장 잘 요약한 것은? [2.7점]
① Transportation technology has become more efficient through automation and digital innovation.
② Subway maps mainly rely on visual techniques to improve route recognition for drivers.
③ Public signs are designed primarily to assist international travelers unfamiliar with local languages.
④ Modern architecture has influenced the design of public transportation facilities.
⑤ Universal design enhances accessibility in transportation systems by accommodating the needs of diverse users.
[1~2] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.

Is it impossible to build an environment where everyone can use products and facilities conveniently and without limitations? ( A ) It was Ronald Mace who sought the answer to this question. ( B ) He contracted polio at the age of nine and spent the rest of his life in a wheelchair. ( C ) Polio is a disease caused by a viral infection and primarily affects the nervous system, leading to muscle paralysis. ( D ) When studying architecture at university, he struggled to access some campus facilities due to inaccessible building designs. ( E ) This experience later inspired him to invent the term universal design, which refers to design for all. As an architect and product designer, he pursued a world in which all products and environments were designed to be artistic and usable to the greatest extent possible by everyone, regardless of their age, size, disability, nationality, or language.
윗글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은? [2.3점]
① (A)     ② (B)     ③ (C)     ④ (D)     ⑤ (E)
윗글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.3점]
① Universal design originated from personal experience and expanded into an inclusive design philosophy.
② Physical limitations can be overcome through individual effort.
③ Accessibility issues occur only in a limited number of facilities.
④ Artistic value and usability are difficult to pursue simultaneously.
⑤ Disability is more a matter of social systems than architectural design.
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
Neil: It seems to get more difficult as we learn more about stocks. So how do we invest in the stock market?

Beth: You can buy stocks through an official place called a stock exchange, or stock market, where you can easily buy or sell stocks in a company. You ,might think investing in stocks is an easy way to make a profit. But if you are investing, you must be prepared to lose money. Since the market constantly fluctuates, there is a risk of loss and debt.
Neil: Investing in stocks is challenging! I bet our listeners are curious about the best investment options though.

Beth: That depends on individual circumstances. Generally, it would be smart to invest in something that interests you, such as a company behind some products you are into. Always remember to do your research, stay informed about the companies you invest in, and be mindful of your risk tolerance.
Neil: Investing can be a powerful tool for building wealth, but it’s essential to approach it with knowledge and caution.
Beth: Wise words, Neil.
Stock investment can be a useful way to build wealth, but it requires careful ____(A)____ and an awareness of potential ____(B)____.
① preparation		risks
② preparation		stability
③ interest		success
④ interest		profits
⑤ confidence    	gains
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [4.5점]

Let’s start with the concept of a stock. A stock is a partial share of ownership in a company. When you buy a stock, you get a portion of the company’s ownership. To put it simply, owning one stock is  _____________________. This does not mean that stockholders themselves can actively participate in the management of the company. Management is generally carried out by professional managers. However, companies hold stockholder meetings to seek the opinions of major stockholders when they make important decisions.
① gaining complete control over a company
② managing a company’s daily operations
③ owning only a part of a company
④ making all important business decisions
⑤ being responsible for the company’s profits and losses
[5~6] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.

Companies are constantly influenced by market factors such as raw material prices, advances in production technology, and labor costs. For example, in terms of raw material prices, if the price of rubber rises, a shoe company may have to pay more to import the rubber it needs from abroad to manufacture sneakers. This, in turn, affects production costs and leads to higher prices in the consumer market. As consumers hesitate to purchase the company’s sneakers, the company may suffer from poor performance, leading to a decline in the stock price. In addition, investors may be concerned about a company’s leadership or reputation. Nowadays, more and more people support companies that prioritize public values such as business transparency, environmental friendliness, and social justice. By purchasing such stocks, investors pursue not only their financial goals but also contribute to building a more sustainable economic system that benefits society as a whole. All these variables can cause daily changes in stock prices in the stock market.
윗글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.3점]
① to explain how various market and social factors affect stock prices
② to criticize unethical behavior by investors
③ to encourage consumers to purchase a specific product
④ to emphasize the importance of technological innovation
⑤ to list cases of corporate management failure
윗글의 논지를 적용한 사례로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
① Regardless of raw material prices, all companies’ stock prices rise in the same way.
② Consumer demand remains unchanged regardless of a company’s performance.
③ Increases in production costs always raise corporate profits.
④ Companies that emphasize ethical management attract greater interest from investors.
⑤ Changes in stock prices occur solely as a result of internal corporate decisions.
다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은? [2.3점]

Too many officials in troubled cities wrongly imagine that they can lead their city back to its former glories with some massive construction project ― a new stadium or light rail system, a convention center, or a housing project. ( A ) With very few exceptions, no public policy can slow the tidal forces of urban change. ( B ) We mustn’t ignore the needs of the poor people who live in the Rust Belt, but public policy should help poor people, not poor places. ( C ) Public policies include optimal resource allocation policies, income redistribution policies, and economic stabilization policies to stabilize the economy. ( D ) Shiny new real estate may dress up a declining city, but it doesn’t solve its underlying problems. The hallmark of declining cities is that they have too much housing and infrastructure relative to the strength of their economies. ( E ) With all that supply of structure and so little demand, it makes no sense to use public money to build more supply. The folly of building-centric urban renewal reminds us that cities aren’t structures; cities are people.
① (A)   ② (B)   ③ (C)   ④ (D)   ⑤ (E)
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은? [2.3점]

Many marine species including oysters, marsh grasses, and fish were deliberately introduced for food or for erosion control, with ⓐa little knowledge of the impacts they could have. Fish and shellfish have been intentionally ⓑintroduced all over the world for aquaculture, providing food and jobs, but they can escape and become a threat to native species, ecosystem function, or livelihoods. Atlantic salmon are ⓒreared in ocean net-pens in Washington State and British Columbia. Many escape each year, and they have been recovered in both saltwater and freshwater in Washington State, British Columbia, and Alaska. Recreational fishing can also spread invasive species. Bait worms from Maine are popular throughout the country. They are commonly packed in seaweed which contains many other organisms. If the seaweed is ⓓdiscarded, it or the organisms on it can colonize new areas. Fishing boots, recreational boats, and trailers can pick up organisms at one location and ⓔmove them elsewhere.
① ⓐ   ② ⓑ   ③ ⓒ   ④ ⓓ    ⑤ ⓔ
다음 글에서 ‘bull market’에 대한 설명으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.3점]

A bull market is a rising stock market situation in which economic conditions are favorable to investors. They include high employment rates, GDP increases, and other positive economic indicators. Think of a charging bull in a field raising its horns. In a bull market, investors often believe in the market’s present and future performance. As such, they increase their stock purchases and maintain their investments.
① an unstable market in which price fluctuations increase due to a surge in short-term speculation
② a market in which only a specific industry grows rapidly while the overall market remains stagnant
③ a market situation in which stock prices generally rise because economic conditions are favorable to investors
④ a declining market phase in which trading is restricted by government regulations
⑤ a market dominated by investor sentiment to avoid high-risk assets
[10~11] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.

The creative team exhibits paradoxical characteristics. It shows tendencies of thought and action ⓐthat we’d assume to be mutually exclusive or contradictory. For example, to do ⓑtheir best work, a team needs deep knowledge of subjects relevant to the problem it’s trying to solve, and a mastery of the processes ⓒinvolved. But at the same time, the team needs fresh perspectives that are unencumbered by the prevailing wisdom or established ways of doing things. Often ⓓcalled a “beginner’s mind,” this is the newcomers’ perspective: people who are curious, even playful, and willing to ask anything — no matter how naive the question may seem — because they don’t know what they don’t know. Thus, ⓔbringing together contradictory characteristics can ______________ the process of new ideas.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ중 어법상 틀린 것은? [2.3점]
① ⓐ   ② ⓑ   ③ ⓒ   ④ ⓓ    ⑤ ⓔ
윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
① accelerate
② estimate
③ evaluate
④ determine
⑤ recognize
[16~17] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오. [30번]

Human innovation in agriculture has unlocked modifications in apples, tulips, and potatoes that never would have been realized through a plant’s natural reproductive cycles. ( A ) This cultivation process has created some of the recognizable vegetables and fruits consumers look for in their grocery stores. ( B ) For example, a million people died over the course of three years during the Irish potato famine because the Irish relied primarily on potatoes and milk to create a nutritionally balanced meal. ( C ) In order to continue its symbiotic relationship with cultivated plants, humanity must allow for biodiversity and recognize the potential  drawbacks that monocultures of plants can introduce. ( D ) Planting seeds of all kinds, even if they don’t seem immediately useful or profitable, can  ensure the longevity of those plants for generations to come. ( E ) A balance must be struck between nature’s capacity for wildness and humanity’s desire for control.
윗글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오. [3.1점]
However, relying on only a few varieties of cultivated crops can leave humankind vulnerable to starvation and agricultural loss if a harvest is destroyed.
① (A)   ② (B)   ③ (C)   ④ (D)   ⑤ (E)
윗글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.3점]
① agriculture directly and indirectly related to human development
② innovation in agriculture through variety improvement
③ the need to eat nutritionally balanced meals
④ production of agricultural products through variety improvement
⑤ problems and solutions of single cultivation through variety improvement
다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]

Relativity works as a general mechanism for the mind, in many ways and across many different areas of life. ___________(A)__________, Brian Wansink, author of Mindless Eating, showed that it can also affect our waistlines. We decide how much to eat not simply as a function of how much food we actually consume, but by a comparison to its alternatives. Say we have to choose between three burgers on a menu, at 8, 10, and 12 ounces. We are likely to pick the 10-ounce burger and be perfectly satisfied at the end of the meal. __________(B)__________, if our options are instead 10, 12, and 14-ounces, we are likely again to choose the middle one, and again feel equally happy and satisfied with the 12-ounce burger at the end of the meal, even though we ate more, which we did not need in order to get our daily nourishment or in order to feel full.
① Similarly		Thus
② Likewise		Similarly
③ For example		However
④ Nevertheless		In short
⑤ On the contrary	In addition
다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것을 2개 고르면? [2.7점]

Before the fancy high-rises, financial headquarters, tourist centers, and souvenir peddlers made their way to Battery Park City, the area behind the World Trade Center was a giant, gross landfill. In 1982, artist Agnes Denes decided to return that landfill back to its roots, although temporarily. Denes was commissioned by the Public Art Fund to create one of the most significant and fantastical pieces of public work Manhattan has ever seen. Her concept was not a traditional sculpture, but a living installation that changed the way the public looked at art. In the name of art, Denes put a beautiful golden wheat field right in the shadow of the gleaming Twin Towers. For Wheatfield ― A Confrontation, Denes and volunteers removed trash from four acres of land, then planted amber waves of grain atop the area. After months of farming and irrigation, the wheat field was thriving and ready. The artist and her volunteers harvested thousands of pounds of wheat to give to food banks in the city, nourishing both the minds and bodies of New Yorkers.
① Denes was the one who asked Public Art Fund to create magnificant public work.
② Dene’s work was directed toward creating a living installation instead of a conventional sculpture.
③ Denes purposely selected the location due to its proximity to Wall Street renowned for poverty and wilderness.
④ Denes and volunteers planted grains on top of the massive trash.
⑤ The harvest from the wheat field was donated to food bank in the city.
Bright Future Walkathon에 관한 다음 안내문의 내용과 일치하는 것은? [2.3점]
Bright Future Walkathon
Sunny Side Foundation is hosting the annual Bright Future Walkathon in support of people in need.
Date & Place
●Date: Saturday, September 25th (Start Time: 9:00 a.m.)
● Place: Green Brook Park
Registration
●All registration fees will be donated to local charities.
●Register online at www.ssfwalkathon.com.
Course (Choose one)
●Course A: 3km (all ages welcome)
●Course B: 5km (for ages 15 and older)
Details
●Each participant who completes the course will receive a T-shirt.
●No refund will be made for cancellations.
① Walkathon의 코스 2가지 모두 참여할 수 있다.
② 등록 취소 시 등록비 환불이 가능하다.
③ Bright Future Walkathon은 매월 열린다.
④ 대회 등록 시 티셔츠를 받을 수 있다.
⑤ 등록비는 지역 자선단체에 기부될 것이다.
[22~23] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오. [36번]

When trying to sustain an independent ethos, cultures face a problem of critical mass. No single individual, acting on his or her own, can produce an ethos. ( A ) This cluster of produced meaning may require some degree of insulation from larger and wealthier outside forces. ( B ) The Canadian Inuit maintain their own ethos, even though they number no more than twenty-four thousand. ( C ) They manage this feat through a combination of trade, to support their way of life, and geographic isolation. ( D ) The Inuit occupy remote territory, removed from major population centers of Canada. If cross-cultural contact were to become sufficiently close, the Inuit ethos would disappear. ( E ) Distinct cultural groups of similar size do not, in the long run, persist in downtown Toronto, Canada, where they come in contact with many outside influences and pursue essentially Western paths for their lives.
윗글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오. [3.1점]
Rather, an ethos results from the interdependent acts of many individuals.
① (A)   ② (B)   ③ (C)   ④ (D)   ⑤ (E)
윗글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.3점]
① Ethnic spirit is a cultural characteristic that continues to be shared.
② Native people are characterized by geographical isolation.
③ Cultural contact will confuse the Inuit society.
④ Ethnicity is the result of cultural interaction.
⑤ An ethos is maintained through disconnection from the outside world.
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.1점]
People also had to hunt down animals or gather plants for their food, and that took a lot of calories.

Deep-fried foods are tastier than bland foods, and children and adults develop a taste for such foods. Fatty foods cause the brain to release oxytocin, a powerful hormone with a calming, antistress, and relaxing influence, said to be the opposite of adrenaline, into the blood stream; hence the term “comfort foods.” ( A ) We may even be genetically programmed to eat too much. For thousands of years, food was very scarce. Food, along with salt, carbs, and fat, was hard to get, and the more you got, the better. ( B ) All of these things are necessary nutrients in the human diet, and when their availability was limited, you could never get too much. ( C ) It’s different these days. We have food at every turn ― lots of those fast-food places and grocery stores with carry-out food. ( D ) But that ingrained “caveman mentality” says that we can’t ever get too much to eat. ( E ) So craving for “unhealthy” food may actually be our body’s attempt to stay healthy.
① (A)   ② (B)   ③ (C)   ④ (D)   ⑤ (E)
[20~21] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오. [35번]

Nurses hold a pivotal position in the mental health care structure and are placed at the centre of the communication network, partly because of their high degree of contact with patients, but also because they have well-developed relationships with other professionals.

(A) This involves translating communication between groups into language that is acceptable and ⓐ[comprehensive / comprehensible] to people who have different ways of understanding mental health problems.
(B) This is a highly ⓑ[sensible / sensitive] and skilled task, requiring a high level of attention to alternative views and a high level of understanding of communication.
(C) Because of this, nurses play a crucial role in interdisciplinary communication. They have a ⓒ[meditating / mediating] role between the various groups of professionals and the patient and carer.
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [2.9점]
윗글 (ⓐ), (ⓑ), (ⓒ)의 각 괄호 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
① comprehensive	sensible		mediating
② comprehensive	sensitive		meditating
③comprehensible	sensible		meditating
④comprehensible	sensitive		mediating
⑤comprehensible	sensitive		meditating
< 서 술 형>
※ 반드시 서술형 답지에 기록하세요.
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말을 본문의 단어를 활용하여 쓰시오. [6점, 부분점수 있음]

In this day and age, it is difficult to imagine our lives without email. But how often do we consider the environmental impact of these virtual messages? At first glance, digital messages appear to save resources. Unlike traditional letters, no paper or stamps are needed; nothing has to be packaged or transported. Many of us tend to assume that using email requires little more than the electricity used to power our computers. It is easy to overlook the invisible energy usage involved in running the network ― particularly when it comes to sending and storing data. Every single email in every single inbox in the world is stored on a server. The incredible quantity of data requires huge server farms ― gigantic centres with millions of computers which store and transmit information. These servers consume massive amounts of energy, 24 hours a day, and require countless litres of water, orair conditioning systems, for cooling. The more messages we send, receive and store, the more servers are needed ― which means more energy consumed, and more carbon emissions. Clearly, sending and receiving electronic messages in an environmentally conscious manner is by no means enough to stop climate change. But with a few careful, mindful changes, unnecessary CO2 emissions can easily be avoided.
Although it is (A)__________ that emails save resources, the (B)__________ of energy by servers for data (C)__________ leads to an increase in carbon emissions.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 우리말 (A)를 다음의 조건에 따라 쓰시오. [4점, 부분점수 있음]

(A)당신이 생각했던 것보다 사회의 더 많은 부분에서 universal design이 발견될 수 있다는 사실이 놀랍게 여겨질지도 모른다. However, enough has not been done to accommodate everyone yet. Universal design should be implemented more extensively to promote full participation in the community for a wider range of people. It is time to build more equitable environments that are accessible to everyone. So are you on board to create a universally designed world for all?
universal design / surprise / find /￼ think
<보 기>
[24~25] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.

Music is used to (A)[molding / mold] customer experience and behavior. A study was conducted that explored what impact it has on employees. Results from the study indicate that participants who listen to rhythmic music were inclined to cooperate more irrespective of factors like age, gender, and academic background, (B)[comparing / compared] to those who listened to less rhythmic music. This positive boost in the participants’ willingness to cooperate was induced regardless of whether they liked the music or not. When people are in a more positive state of mind, they tend to become more agreeable and creative, while those on the opposite spectrum tend to focus on their individual problems rather than giving attention to solving group problems. The rhythm of music has a strong pull on people’s behavior. This is (C)[why / because] when people listen to music with a steady pulse, they tend to match their actions to the beat. This translates to better teamwork when making decisions because everyone is following one tempo.
윗글 (A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법상 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.3점]
① molding		comparing		why
② molding		compared		because
③ mold		comparing		because
④ mold		compared		why
⑤ mold		compared		because
윗글에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [2.3점]
① 음악은 고객의 경험과 행동을 형성하는데 사용된다.
② 리듬감 있는 음악을 듣는 참가자는 나이에 상관없이 더 협력했다.
③ 참가자들의 협력은 음악의 선호도에 따라서 차이가 있었다.
④ 사람들은 긍정적인 마음에 있을 때 더 창의적인 경향이 있었다.
⑤ 음악의 리듬은 사람들의 행동을 강하게 끌어당긴다.
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.1점]
However, he wasn’t interested in her dance.

There once lived a girl named Melanie. She wanted to be a ballet dancer. One day, Melanie’s mother saw her dancing with the flawless steps and enthusiasm of a ballerina. “Isn’t it strange? Melanie is dancing so well without any formal training!” her mother said. ( ① ) “I must get her professional lessons to help her polish her skill.” ( ② ) The following day, Melanie accompanied her mother to a local dance institute. ( ③ ) Upon meeting the dance teacher, Mr. Edler, her mother requested to admit Melanie to his institute. ( ④ ) The teacher asked Melanie to audition. She was happy and showed him some of her favorite dance steps. ( ⑤ ) He was busy with other tasks in the dance room. “You can leave now! The girl is just average. Don’t let her waste her time aspiring to be a dancer,” he said. Melanie and her mother were shocked to hear this.
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말을 본문의 단어를 활용하여 쓰시오. [6점, 부분점수 있음]

Organisms living in the deep sea have adapted to the high pressure by storing water in their bodies, some consisting almost entirely of water. Most deep-sea organisms lack gas bladders. They are cold-blooded organisms that adjust their body temperature to their environment, allowing them to survive in the cold water while maintaining a low metabolism. Many species lower their metabolism so much that they are able to survive without food for long periods of time, as finding the sparse food that is available expends a lot of energy. Many predatory fish of the deep sea are equipped with enormous mouths and sharp teeth, enabling them to hold on to prey and overpower it. Some predators hunting in the residual light zone of the ocean have excellent visual capabilities, while others are able to create their own light to attract prey or a mating partner.

Deep-sea organisms survive extreme environments through the (A)__________ of their body temperature and a(n) (B)__________ metabolism, while some also rely on the (C)__________ of their own light for hunting and mating.
다음 편지를 쓴 목적을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 적으시오. [4점, 부분점수 있음]
Dear parents and students of Douglas School,

As you know, our school was built over 150 years ago. While we are proud of our school’s history, the facilities are not exactly what they should be for modern schooling. Thanks to a generous donation to the school foundation, we will be able to start renovating those parts of our campus that have become outdated. We hope this will help provide our students with the best education possible. I’m writing to inform you that the auditorium will be the first building closed for repairs. Philosophical activity is based on the recognition of ignorance. The philosopher’s thirst for knowledge is shown through attempts to find better answers to questions even if those answers are never found. At the same time, a philosopher also knows that being too sure can hinder the discovery of other and better possibilities. In a philosophical dialogue, the participants are aware that there are things they do not know or understand. The goal of the dialogue is to arrive at a conception that one did not know or understand beforehand. In traditional schools, where philosophy is not present, students often work with factual questions, they learn specific content listed in the curriculum, and they are not required to solve philosophical problems. However, we know that awareness of what one does not know can be a good way to acquire knowledge. Knowledge and understanding are developed through thinking and talking. Putting things into words makes things clearer. Therefore, students must not be afraid of saying something wrong or talking without first being sure that they are right.
